newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian farmers lift Milan airport blockade.
newsitem.headline: Italian farmers lift Milan airport blockade.

text.p: Milan's Linate airport reopened following a two-hour shutdown on Friday after protesting dairy farmers were warned that the police would step in if they did not lift barriers obstructing road access.
Flights resumed shortly after 1730 GMT after some 30 flights had been diverted to other airports and 10 cancelled.
Earlier aviation authorities said they were closing Linate airport for a week after protesting farmers blocked road access, placing the airport's emergency services in jeopardy.

Dairy farmers set up blockades around northern Italy's busiest airport to protest against EU fines imposed on them for exceeding strict milk quotas. Farmers have also thrown up road blocks at Milan's second airport, Malpensa, and Venice airport.
Road traffic in Pavia, 40 km (25 miles) south of Milan, ground to a halt when some 50 farmers drove their tractors into the town centre.
The deputy director at Linate, Vincenzo Fusco, told Reuters earlier that Linate airport would be shut for up to a week but said the airport could be re-opened at any time if the blockade were lifted.
"The airport has been closed because access roads were blocked and in the event of any accident we would not have been able to organise a rescue operation," he said.
Fusco said the blockade had been preventing air-traffic controllers and firemen from getting to work on time.
The city prefect immediately served warning on the dairy farmers that the authorities would restore order if they persisted with their blockade.

"If illegality should persist notwithstanding all the good will shown at central level, we will have to intervene forcefully to restore conditions of public security," said Roberto Sorge, the central government's senior representative in Milan.
A spokesman for the dairy workers later said traffic was now being waved through along the main road to Linate but pickets were still on stand-by to resume the blockade.
Italian dairy farmers have been hit with some 370 billion lire ($235 million) of fines, which have to be paid by the end of the month, for exceeding milk quotas.

They want the government to pay the levies and have camped out in Milan for nine days to press their case. The farmers closed access to the airports on Friday after Prime Minister Romano Prodi reiterated that the state would not pay the fines.
The farmers also threatened to block motorways across the north of Italy to force Prime Minister Romano Prodi to accept their demands.
"We are tired and we want to put pressure on the government," the farmers' unofficial leader Aldo Bettinelli told reporters in Milan.
Hundreds of tractors snarled traffic around Venice's Marco Polo airport, while passengers trying to reach Linate airport were forced to walk the final kilometre to the terminal.
Farmers also sealed roads around Milan's international airport Malpensa, where tractors have been building up all week in preparation for the blockade.
They had shut off Linate airport last week, but opened the roads again on Monday after Prodi promised to hear their grievances.
Prodi said on Friday he would open an inquiry into the contested milk quotas, but the farmers said on Friday that was not enough.
Paolo Micolini, chairman of the small farmers' association Coldiretti, said talks with the centre-left government were now on ice after an inconclusive meeting with Prodi.
